mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor of 20-day returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or average 20-day return in declining FEDFUNDS periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 5-day S&P 500 return in UNRATE > 5.5% periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for UNRATE as predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand and business investment, jointly driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term between HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce significant Rank IC (below 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or average 20-day return when both rise is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits and increases recession risk, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day S&P 500 return during INDPRO < 100 periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for INDPRO as predictor of 60-day returns in contraction regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong residential demand and economic expansion that consistently boosts corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST as predictor of 5-day returns falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or average 5-day return in rising HOUST periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% indicates monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day S&P 500 return in FEDFUNDS > 0.5% periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, jointly driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term between PAYEMS and UNRATE fails to produce significant Rank IC (below 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or average 5-day return when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth exceeding 1.5% annualized (GDPC1 growth rate) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day S&P 500 return during GDPC1 growth rate > 1.5% periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC for GDPC1 growth rate as predictor of 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
